direction-type.words: Oh cam' doon the stair, pretty Peggy my dear. Cam' doon the stair pretty Peggy-oh.
Oh cam' doon the stairs, and comb back your yella hair. Tak' a last farewell tae your daddy-oh.
Oh I'll gi'e ye ribbons fine for your bonnie, golden hair. An' I'll gi'e ye a necklace o' amber-oh.
I'll gi'e ye silken petticoats befittin' your degree. If ye'll cam' wi' me tae my chamber-oh.
Oh I hae ribbons fine for my bonnie, golden hair. And I ha'e a necklace o' amber-oh.
An' I ha'e petticoats a-befittin' my degree. An' I'd be scorned if seen in your chamber-oh.
'Twis early the next mornin' fin we rode awa'. And oh but oor captain was sorry-oh.
The drums they did beat o'er the bonny braes o' Gight. And the band played 'The Lowlands O' Fyvie-oh'.
Lang eer we went intae auld Meldrum toon. It's we had tae carry oor captain-oh.
Lang eer we went intae bonnie Aberdeen, It's we had oor captain tae bury-oh.
Green grow the birks o' bonny Ythanside. And low lie the lowlands o' Fyvie-oh.
Oor captain's name was Ned, and he died for a maid. He died for the bonnie maid o' Fyvie-oh.
